c74object.name: syncSuite.scoreplayer
c74object.digest: Utility for designing, managing and triggering cues.
c74object.description: This abstraction is based on the qlist object, allowing for simpler score writing and also more complex functionalities.

inlet.digest: Messages controlling score loading and playback position
inlet.description: Accepts the "read", "open", "autowatch", "skip", "next", "rewind", "cue" and "event" messages described below. There is no bare-number shorthand for "cue"/"event" - a plain int sent to this inlet is not treated as a cue number.

outlet.description: Outputs the numeric index of the cue or event currently positioned/playing.
Outputs the name string of the cue or event currently positioned/playing.

outlet.digest: Delay monitor: 1 while a scheduled delay is pending
outlet.description: Outputs 1 while a message delay (see the score file format under "read") is pending and "next" is therefore blocked, and 0 once the delay has resolved. During a delay, no other event can be triggered.

outlet.digest: Cue/event names, for building a cue-selector menu
outlet.description: Outputs the full list of cue/event names each time a score is (re)loaded, intended to fill a "umenu" elsewhere in the patch so the user can build a custom cue-selection interface.

objarg.name: read
objarg.digest: Score file to load at creation time
objarg.description: Sets the @read attribute at creation time: the path of a score ".txt" file to load immediately, equivalent to sending "read <path>" right after instantiation. Optional; if omitted, no score is loaded until a "read"/"open" message is sent.

method.name: read
method.description: With a "filename" argument (a score ".txt" file), loads that file directly, replacing any previously loaded score. With no argument, opens a file-choose dialog to select one. On success, a message confirming the score name and cue count is posted to the Max window, and the cue/event names are output out the fourth outlet.

method.name: open
method.description: Opens a text editor window on the currently loaded score file, letting it be edited directly. Saving from this editor reloads the score automatically if "autowatch" is enabled.

method.name: autowatch
method.digest: Enables or disables auto-reload on save
method.description: Turns the @autowatch behavior on (1) or off (0): when on, the loaded score file is automatically reloaded whenever it is saved, from the "open" editor or any other text editor. Equivalent to setting the @autowatch attribute.

method.name: skip
method.digest: Sets whether jumping to a cue/event executes the messages in between
method.description: Equivalent to setting the @skip attribute: when on (1, default), jumping to a cue or event via "cue"/"event" does not execute the messages of the cues/events skipped over. When off (0), jumping executes every message from the current position through the target, including any delays. "next" always executes messages normally, regardless of this setting.

method.name: next
method.description: Advances to and plays the next cue/event in sequence, sending all of its messages (in order, honoring any delays - see "read"). Blocked while a delay from the current cue is still pending; see the delay-monitor outlet.

method.name: rewind
method.digest: Resets playback to the start of the score
method.description: Resets the current position to the beginning of the score, equivalent to "cue 0" / "event 0".

method.name: cue
method.digest: Selects a cue by index, without triggering it
method.description: Positions the player one cue before "index" (1-based; 0 behaves like "rewind"), waiting for a subsequent "next" message to actually trigger it. Whether the messages of the cues skipped over on the way are executed depends on "skip" (see above). "event" is an exact synonym for this message.

method.name: event
method.description: Identical to "cue": positions the player one event before "index", waiting for "next" to trigger it. Provided as a separate name for compatibility with the EVENT keyword used in score files (originally for antescofo~-style score compatibility). See "cue" above.

attribute.name: read
attribute.digest: Score file loaded at creation time
attribute.description: Path of a score ".txt" file to load when the object is instantiated. See the "read" message for the file format and behavior. Optional; no default.

attribute.name: autowatch
attribute.digest: Auto-reloads the score file when it is saved
attribute.description: When enabled (1, default), the loaded score file is automatically reloaded whenever it is saved to disk, from the "open" editor or any other text editor. Same as sending the "autowatch" message.

attribute.name: skip
attribute.digest: Whether jumping to a cue skips the messages in between
attribute.description: When enabled (1, default), jumping to a cue/event with "cue"/"event" does not execute the messages of the cues/events in between. When disabled (0), all messages from the current position through the target are executed, including delays. Does not affect "next", which always executes messages normally. Same as sending the "skip" message.

c74object.discussion:
A score is a plain ".txt" file made of cue/event blocks. Each block starts with a declaration line, "CUE <n> <name>" or "EVENT <n> <name>" (the two keywords are exact synonyms), followed by zero or more message lines to send when that cue plays: "<receiver> <message...>", where "<receiver>" is the name of a Max "receive" object elsewhere in the patch. Prefixing a message line with an integer, "<delay-ms> <receiver> <message...>", delays that message (and, once used, every following message in the same cue) by that many milliseconds; no other event can be triggered while a delay is pending. "DO-LINE <receiver> <start> <target> <time-ms>" sends "<receiver>" a linear ramp from "start" to "target" over "time-ms", exactly like the "line" object; up to 20 such ramps can run simultaneously, and unlike delayed messages they do not block "next". Lines beginning with "//" are comments and are not sent.
The send/receive names CUE, EVENT and DO-LINE (case-sensitive) are reserved for this object's internal use - do not reuse them elsewhere in the patch. Only one syncSuite.scoreplayer should exist per patch, since these names are global.
